subject: Penumbra on-prem: sustained rate degradation and p95 latency increase
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@penumbracorp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@penumbracorp.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: spike: increased p95 + error rate since Friday deploy

Hi Evelyn / Marissa —

We started seeing a sustained degradation in our on-prem inference cluster after the Friday model upgrade. Key symptoms:
- p95 latency up from ~210ms to ~820ms for text-generation RPCs
- overall throughput (req/s) down ~30% for steady-state traffic
- error rate (5xx) climbed to 4.7% during peak windows

Attached is a small log snippet and a short perf snapshot (penumbra_log_snippet_0407.txt). We've kept the workload constant and the issue appears correlated with the new model binary and a longer token-window in production.

This is affecting our customer-facing sessions; we need an immediate triage and ETA for mitigation.

Can you confirm if the new quantized variant was routed to the private cluster and whether any kernel/ABI changes rolled with it?

Thanks,
Alex Ruiz
Director, Platform Engineering
Penumbra Software

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: spike: increased p95 + error rate since Friday deploy

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the log. Looping in Ben + Laura to help triage (SRE + PM).

Initial checks I ran:
- Confirmed the on-prem control plane accepted the new model artifact on Friday at 18:21 PDT.
- No infra-level kernel upgrades were applied on the cluster during the window.
- KV cache hit rates dropped ~22% in the morning windows (from our dashboard) which could explain throughput fall.

Immediate ask from our side: can you share the exact model variant name and whether any prompt-prefetching layers changed on your side? I'll start a canary rollback plan and we can attempt KV cache warming + small kernel parameter tweak (spin-wq/batching).

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Temp route 30% of traffic to previous model artifact (canary rollback)
2) Run a manual KV cache flush + targeted warming for hot prefixes
3) Collect a 10-minute flame graph and decode times at token granularity (I'll attach a runbook)

I'll set up a short war room for 10:30 PDT. Ben — can SRE prioritize a kernel parameter probe and capture perf counters?

Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_canary_rollout.md (text/markdown, 4KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@penumbracorp.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:28:45 -0700
Subject: Re: spike: increased p95 + error rate since Friday deploy

Triage notes (quick):
- Replica-level queues show higher lock contention on the attention kernel for sequence lengths >1024. The new model selects a different attention kernel path under those conditions.
- Memory alloc pattern changed; per-GPU allocator fragmentation increased which is consistent with slower encode/decode times and lower req/s.
- perf_snapshot_20270407.csv attached (synthetic traffic run and timeline).

Short-term mitigations we can run in parallel:
- Canary rollback to previous artifact for 30% of requests (low blast radius).
- Apply allocator backpressure tuning (reduce arena size; immediate restart of workers required).
- Temp enable smaller context truncation at the ingress to reduce heavy token windows for top 5 callers.

Longer term: revisit kernel selection heuristics and release a patch to prefer the older attention kernel variant when seq_len distribution skew > 80th percentile.

Ben — please coordinate the worker restarts; Laura, can you own communicating ETA to Penumbra execs?

Marissa Cole
Principal Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Executive heads-up: Penumbra on-prem performance incident

Laura / Markus — putting this on your radar. Penumbra (PNB-4521) is experiencing a notable p95 jump and throughput drop after their Friday model promotion. Marissa's triage indicates attention-kernel and allocator fragmentation artifacts.

Constraints: this is an on-prem deployment; we do not control hardware scaling. Two feasible paths are:
A) Canary rollback to previous artifact for 30% of traffic + cache warming (expected mitigation window 15-45 minutes once started).
B) Push a config-only allocator tweak + worker restart (expected mitigation window 5-20 minutes but requires short (~90s) request drops during restart).

Customer asks for an ETA and an exec-level contact for potential SLA credits if this persists. They'd like a timeline within the next 2 hours. Recommend we authorize both A+B in parallel; Laura, can you confirm an external communication and whether we should pre-clear a temporary credit/exception?

Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
